_comment: Machining calculators — the ONE definition of every machining cycle-time formula. scripts/generate-machining-calculators-migration.mjs writes these into the calculators / calculator_fields / process_calculator_mappings tables; the cost engine evaluates the stored formulas (calculator-formula-evaluator.ts) with CAD + lookup-table inputs; tests load this file as the stand-in for those rows. Edit here and regenerate — never hand-edit the migration. Every calculator's output is 'Cycle Time' in seconds. Input 'source': cad | lookup | machine | bom | drawing | engine | default (a database default with no reference source — shown as such in the trace).

stations.2_axis_bar_feed_lathe_with_sub_spindle: 2 Axis Bar Feed Lathe with Sub Spindle
stations.3_axis_bar_feed_lathe_with_sub_spindle: 3 Axis Bar Feed Lathe with Sub Spindle

calculators.name: Machining - Drilling
calculators.description: Drilled-hole cycle time: CAD hole diameter and depth, cutting speed and feed from tblDrilling for the material and drill construction.

calculators.name: Machining - Drilling
calculators.description: Drilling a hole as the Machining calculator workbook's Drilling sheet times it: n = 1000 v / (pi D), capped at the machine's spindle limit; time = (hole depth + 10 mm) / (feed x n), rounded up to whole seconds a hole. Cutting speed (a range, picked at the Range Position) and the feed of the hole diameter's band from the workbook's drilling and reaming table for the material; drill price and life from the sheet.

fields.name: Range Position
fields.note: The workbook gives cutting speeds as ranges ('75 - 110' m/min). 0.5 takes the middle of each range; 0 its low end, 1 its high end.

fields.name: Max Spindle Speed
fields.note: The selected machine's own top spindle speed (mhr_records.specs spindle_speed_rpm, migration 1136). The workbook has no cap.

fields.name: Approach Length
fields.note: the Machining calculator workbook (memory/Machining - Calculator Database (1).xlsx), Drilling sheet: the length of cut plus 10 mm for the tool's approach and overrun.

calculators.name: Machining - Rough Turning
calculators.description: Rough turning passes over the turned length: CAD turned diameter/length, stock bar diameter, depth of cut / speed / feed from tblGeneralTurning.

fields.name: Rough Stock
fields.formula: max({Radial Stock} - min({Finish Depth of Cut}, {Radial Stock}), 0)

calculators.name: Machining - Rough Turning
calculators.description: Rough turning from the bar down to the diameter the finish cut starts at, timed as the Machining calculator workbook's Turning sheet times a cut: spindle speed from the diameter the cut starts at (the bar), passes = (bar diameter - finish start diameter) / (2 x depth of cut), each pass the turned length plus the approach at the feed rate. CAD turned diameter/length, stock bar diameter, depth of cut / speed / feed from tblGeneralTurning; the 10 mm approach is the workbook's.

fields.name: Approach Length
fields.note: The reference data has no approach distance for turning. The Machining calculator workbook (Machining - Calculator Database, Turning sheet) adds 10 mm to the length of cut for the tool's approach and overrun: machining time = pi x D x (L + 10) / (1000 x v x s) x passes.

fields.name: Finish Start Diameter
fields.formula: min({Turned Diameter} + 2 * {Finish Depth of Cut}, {Bar Diameter})

fields.name: Rough Passes
fields.formula: ({Bar Diameter} - {Finish Start Diameter}) / (2 * {Rough Depth of Cut})

calculators.name: Machining - Rough Turning
calculators.description: Rough turning from the bar down to the diameter the finish cut starts at, as the Machining calculator workbook's Turning sheet times it: n = 1000 v / (pi D) at the bar diameter, capped at the machine's spindle limit; passes = (bar - finish start diameter) / (2 x depth of cut), rounded up to whole passes (the sheet leaves a fraction); time = (turned length + 10 mm) / (feed x n) x passes, rounded up to whole seconds. Cutting speed and feed from the workbook's Turning cutting conditions (carbide, the band holding the depth of cut), picked at the Range Position.

fields.name: Rough Depth of Cut
fields.note: the Machining calculator workbook (memory/Machining - Calculator Database (1).xlsx), Turning sheet: depth of cut t = 2 mm in its worked rows (H8:H10).

fields.name: Finish Depth of Cut
fields.note: the Machining calculator workbook (memory/Machining - Calculator Database (1).xlsx), Facing and Internal Boring sheets: depth of cut 0.5 mm, the finishing cut.

fields.name: Range Position
fields.note: The workbook gives cutting speeds and feeds as ranges (Turning cutting conditions: '120 - 200' m/min). 0.5 takes the middle of each range; 0 its low end, 1 its high end.

fields.name: Max Spindle Speed
fields.note: The selected machine's own top spindle speed (mhr_records.specs spindle_speed_rpm, migration 1136, from memory/machining/machine). The workbook has no cap; a machine cannot turn faster than its spindle.

fields.name: Approach Length
fields.note: the Machining calculator workbook (memory/Machining - Calculator Database (1).xlsx), Turning sheet: the length of cut plus 10 mm for the tool's approach and overrun.

fields.name: Rough Cutting Speed
fields.formula: {Rough Speed Min} + {Range Position} * ({Rough Speed Max} - {Rough Speed Min})

fields.name: Rough Feed
fields.formula: {Rough Feed Min} + {Range Position} * ({Rough Feed Max} - {Rough Feed Min})

fields.name: Finish Start Diameter
fields.formula: min({Turned Diameter} + 2 * {Finish Depth of Cut}, {Bar Diameter})

fields.name: Rough Passes
fields.formula: ceil(({Bar Diameter} - {Finish Start Diameter}) / (2 * {Rough Depth of Cut}))

fields.name: Spindle Speed
fields.formula: min({Max Spindle Speed}, {Rough Cutting Speed} * 1000 / (pi * {Bar Diameter}))

calculators.name: Machining - Finish Turning
calculators.description: One finish turning pass over the turned length: CAD turned diameter/length, finish speed and feed from tblGeneralTurning.

calculators.name: Machining - Finish Turning
calculators.description: One finish turning pass over the turned length, timed as the Machining calculator workbook's Turning sheet times a cut: spindle speed from the diameter the cut starts at (the turned diameter plus the finish depth of cut on each side, never more than the bar), the turned length plus the approach at the feed rate. CAD turned diameter/length, stock bar diameter, depth of cut / speed / feed from tblGeneralTurning; the 10 mm approach is the workbook's.

fields.name: Approach Length
fields.note: The reference data has no approach distance for turning. The Machining calculator workbook (Machining - Calculator Database, Turning sheet) adds 10 mm to the length of cut for the tool's approach and overrun: machining time = pi x D x (L + 10) / (1000 x v x s) x passes.

fields.name: Finish Start Diameter
fields.formula: min({Turned Diameter} + 2 * {Finish Depth of Cut}, {Bar Diameter})

calculators.name: Machining - Finish Turning
calculators.description: One finish turning pass over the turned length, as the Machining calculator workbook's Turning sheet times a cut: n = 1000 v / (pi D) at the diameter the cut starts at (turned diameter + 2 x finish depth, never more than the bar), capped at the machine's spindle limit; time = (turned length + 10 mm) / (feed x n), rounded up to whole seconds. Cutting speed and feed from the workbook's Turning cutting conditions (carbide, the band holding the finish depth of cut), picked at the Range Position.

fields.name: Finish Depth of Cut
fields.note: the Machining calculator workbook (memory/Machining - Calculator Database (1).xlsx), Facing and Internal Boring sheets: depth of cut 0.5 mm, the finishing cut.

fields.name: Range Position
fields.note: The workbook gives cutting speeds and feeds as ranges (Turning cutting conditions: '120 - 200' m/min). 0.5 takes the middle of each range; 0 its low end, 1 its high end.

fields.name: Max Spindle Speed
fields.note: The selected machine's own top spindle speed (mhr_records.specs spindle_speed_rpm, migration 1136, from memory/machining/machine). The workbook has no cap; a machine cannot turn faster than its spindle.

fields.name: Approach Length
fields.note: the Machining calculator workbook (memory/Machining - Calculator Database (1).xlsx), Turning sheet: the length of cut plus 10 mm for the tool's approach and overrun.

fields.name: Finish Cutting Speed
fields.formula: {Finish Speed Min} + {Range Position} * ({Finish Speed Max} - {Finish Speed Min})

fields.name: Finish Feed
fields.formula: {Finish Feed Min} + {Range Position} * ({Finish Feed Max} - {Finish Feed Min})

fields.name: Finish Start Diameter
fields.formula: min({Turned Diameter} + 2 * {Finish Depth of Cut}, {Bar Diameter})

fields.name: Spindle Speed
fields.formula: min({Max Spindle Speed}, {Finish Cutting Speed} * 1000 / (pi * {Finish Start Diameter}))

calculators.name: Machining - Parting
calculators.description: Part-off plunge from the bar surface to its centre: stock bar diameter, insert speed and feed from tblVirtualPartoffInsertCutData.

calculators.name: Machining - Parting
calculators.description: Part-off plunge from the bar surface to its centre, as the Machining calculator workbook's Cutoff sheet times it: n = 1000 v / (pi D) at the bar diameter, capped at the machine's spindle limit; time = (travel + 10 mm) / (feed x n), rounded up to whole seconds. Corrections: the travel is the bar's radius, or a tube's wall (the sheet types 13 mm for a 50 mm bar), and speed and feed are the part-off insert's own (tblVirtualPartoffInsertCutData; the sheet's 18 m/min and 0.8 'feed per tooth' are not a part-off insert's). Tool price and life from the sheet.

fields.name: Bore Diameter
fields.note: A tube's bore: its part-off cuts through the wall only. 0 for a solid bar.

fields.name: Max Spindle Speed
fields.note: The selected machine's own top spindle speed (mhr_records.specs spindle_speed_rpm, migration 1136, from memory/machining/machine). The workbook has no cap; a machine cannot turn faster than its spindle.

fields.name: Approach Length
fields.note: the Machining calculator workbook (memory/Machining - Calculator Database (1).xlsx), Cutoff sheet: the length of cut plus 10 mm for the tool's approach and overrun.

calculators.name: Machining - Reaming
calculators.description: Reaming pass through the drilled hole: CAD hole diameter and depth, speed and feed from tblReaming.

calculators.name: Machining - Reaming
calculators.description: Reaming a drilled hole as the Machining calculator workbook's Reaming sheet times it: n = 1000 v / (pi D), capped at the machine's spindle limit; time = (hole depth + 4 mm + the point length (D / 2) x 0.577) / (feed x n), rounded up to whole seconds a hole. Cutting speed and the feed of the hole diameter's band from the workbook's drilling and reaming table for the material. The workbook prices no reamer.

fields.name: Range Position
fields.note: The workbook gives cutting speeds as ranges ('75 - 110' m/min). 0.5 takes the middle of each range; 0 its low end, 1 its high end.

fields.name: Max Spindle Speed
fields.note: The selected machine's own top spindle speed (mhr_records.specs spindle_speed_rpm, migration 1136). The workbook has no cap.

fields.name: Approach Length
fields.note: the Machining calculator workbook (memory/Machining - Calculator Database (1).xlsx), Reaming sheet: the length of cut plus 4 mm for the tool's approach and overrun.

calculators.name: Machining - Rigid Tapping
calculators.description: Rigid tapping of a threaded hole: CAD thread diameter, depth and pitch (the part, else the ISO 261 coarse pitch of its nominal size), cutting speed from tblTapping for the material and pitch. The tap feeds one pitch per revolution in and reverses out at the same feed.

calculators.name: Machining - Rigid Tapping
calculators.description: Rigid tapping, as the Machining calculator workbook's Tapping sheet times it, corrected: n = 1000 v / (pi D) at the thread's nominal diameter, capped at the machine's spindle limit; the feed is the thread pitch (a tap advances one pitch a turn; the sheet's 0.25 mm/rev and its 122 m/min table are a drilling cut); the tap goes in and back out over the thread depth + 4 mm; rounded up to whole seconds a thread. Cutting speed is the sheet's own HSS tapping speed for the material (Tapping!A33:D58), a range picked at the Range Position. The workbook prices no tap.

fields.name: Range Position
fields.note: The workbook gives cutting speeds as ranges ('75 - 110' m/min). 0.5 takes the middle of each range; 0 its low end, 1 its high end.

fields.name: Max Spindle Speed
fields.note: The selected machine's own top spindle speed (mhr_records.specs spindle_speed_rpm, migration 1136). The workbook has no cap.

fields.name: Approach Length
fields.note: the Machining calculator workbook (memory/Machining - Calculator Database (1).xlsx), Tapping sheet: the length of cut plus 4 mm for the tool's approach and overrun.

calculators.name: Machining - Jig Boring
calculators.description: Jig boring: finish-boring physics from tblBoringV2 repeated the number of passes tblGtolProcessCapabilities gives for jig boring.

calculators.name: Machining - Gun Drilling
calculators.description: Deep-hole gun drilling: CAD hole diameter and depth, speed and feed from tblGunDrilling.

calculators.name: Machining - Deep Bore
calculators.description: Deep-hole boring: CAD hole diameter and depth, speed and feed from the deep bore drill lookup.

calculators.name: Machining - Cylindrical Grinding
calculators.description: Traverse grinding of a turned OD: CAD diameter/length, grinding allowance (variables finishGrindingDepth), wheel/work data from tblCylindricalGrinding.

calculators.name: Machining - Internal Grinding
calculators.description: Traverse grinding of a bore: CAD bore diameter/depth, grinding allowance (variables finishGrindingDepth), wheel/work data from tblInternalGrinding.

calculators.name: Machining - Jig Grind
calculators.description: Jig grinding of a hardened bore: traverse bore-grinding values (tblInternalGrinding; memory/ has no jig-grinding table) repeated the number of passes tblGtolProcessCapabilities gives for jig grinding.

calculators.name: Machining - Surface Grinding
calculators.description: Traverse surface grinding of a flat face on a reciprocating grinder: CAD face length and width, grinding allowance (variables finishGrindingDepth), table speed, down-feeds and crossfeed from tblReciprocatingSurfaceGrinding (crossfeed capped at its fraction of the tblGrinding wheel width). Each pass strokes the face length once per crossfeed step across its width.

calculators.name: Machining - Keyway Broaching
calculators.description: Keyway broaching with the reference broach for the keyway width and length: a pull-type broach (single pass) when one fits, else a shim-type broach (one pass per shim plus the first). Each pass strokes the broach (teeth x pitch) plus the keyway length at the broach cutting speed; the broach is repositioned between passes (variables).

calculators.name: Machining - Wire EDM
calculators.description: One roughing and one finishing wire pass over the CAD cut path, feed rates from tblWireEDMing.

calculators.name: Machining - Deburring
calculators.description: Deburring every sharp edge: CAD sharp-edge length (seams and tangent edges excluded) at the tblDeburring edge speed for the material.

calculators.name: Machining - Index Transfer
calculators.description: Multi-spindle index cycle per part: drum index, transfer, stock feed and speed synchronisation times from the machine record.

fields.name: Cycle Time
fields.formula: {Drum Index Time} + {Transfer Time} + {Stock Feed Time} + {Speed Synchronization Time}

calculators.name: Machining - Secondary Setup
calculators.description: A second chucking for features a 2-axis lathe cannot reach in one setup: workholder install-and-remove time from tblInstallingTurningWorkholders, spread over the batch.

calculators.name: Machining - Inspection
calculators.description: Inspection time per part: per-piece measurement (allowances are database defaults — no reference source maps features to tblInspection analyses), spread over first-article / in-process / final sampling.

fields.name: Tight Tolerance Time
fields.formula: IF({Tightest Tolerance} > 0 and {Tightest Tolerance} <= {Tight Tolerance Threshold}, {Tight Tolerance CMM Time}, 0)

fields.name: Inspection per Piece
fields.formula: {Positioning Time} + {Holes Sampled} * {Time per Sampled Hole} + {Threads Checked} * {Time per Thread Gauge} + {Tight Tolerance Time} + {GDT Time}

fields.name: In-process Pieces
fields.formula: floor(max({Batch Size} - {First Article Pieces}, 0) / {In-process 1 in N})

fields.name: Measured Minutes per Batch
fields.formula: {Inspection per Piece} * ({First Article Pieces} + {In-process Pieces}) + {Final Check Time} * {Final Check Pieces}

calculators.name: Machining - Inspection
calculators.description: Inspection time per part from memory/Machining: one analysis of the default inspection type (variables defaultInspectionType, its time from tblInspection) on the share of parts inspected (variables defaultInspectionSampleRatio), plus every part's final quality inspection (variables defaultFinalInspectionTime, min). The holes inspected (Special Inspection: Feature Inspection of SimpleHole, MultiStepHole, RingedHole) are listed on the line; the reference does not make the time per hole, so one analysis is one inspected part.

fields.name: Cycle Time
fields.formula: {Time Per Analysis} * {Inspection Sample Ratio} + {Final Inspection Time} * 60

calculators.name: Machining - Inspection
calculators.description: Inspection time per part from memory/Machining: one analysis of the default inspection type (variables defaultInspectionType, its time from tblInspection) on the share of parts inspected (variables defaultInspectionSampleRatio), plus every part's final quality inspection (variables defaultFinalInspectionTime, min). The holes inspected (Special Inspection: Feature Inspection of SimpleHole, MultiStepHole, RingedHole) are listed on the line; the reference does not make the time per hole, so one analysis is one inspected part. The inspection gauge's wear is the line's tool cost: its price over its life, from the workbook's Inspection sheet (Rs 3500 over 10 000 parts).

fields.name: Cycle Time
fields.formula: {Time Per Analysis} * {Inspection Sample Ratio} + {Final Inspection Time} * 60

calculators.name: Machining - Hobbing
calculators.description: Hobbing a gear: CAD teeth, face width, module (tip diameter / (teeth + 2)) and tooth depth ((tip - root) / 2); ANSI hob diameter and starts (tblAnsiHobbing, variables defaultNumStarts); cutting speed and axial feed (tblHobbing). The hob travels the face width plus its approach (the chord of a hob of that diameter entering the tooth depth); the gear turns teeth / starts revolutions per hob revolution.

calculators.name: Machining - Shaving
calculators.description: Gear shaving after hobbing: CAD teeth, module and face width; strokes, cutting speed and feed per workpiece revolution from tblShaving; workpiece speed capped at variables maxShavingWorkpieceSpeed. Each stroke traverses the face width.

calculators.name: Machining - Rotary Broaching
calculators.description: Rotary broaching a polygon socket (drawing polygon callout + CAD polygon ring): depth from CAD; RPM and feed from tblRotaryBroaching (depth within the broach reach), feed calibrated by variables rotaryBroachFeedAdjustment. The pilot hole is priced by the Drilling calculator.

calculators.name: Machining - Milling
calculators.description: The milling line of a part on a mill or a live-tool turning machine: the time of every catalog operation the machine performs on the part's CAD features (operation-sequencer.ts), by operation group, plus the allowance for rapid moves and tool changes between them.

fields.name: Cutting Time
fields.formula: {Facing Time} + {Rough Milling Time} + {Finish Milling Time} + {Contouring Time} + {Slot and Groove Milling Time} + {Hole Making Time} + {Edge Treatment Time} + {Other Operations Time}

calculators.name: Machining - Milling
calculators.description: The milling line of a part on a mill or a live-tool turning machine: the time of every catalog operation the machine performs on the part's CAD features (operation-sequencer.ts), by operation group, then the moves between them: a tool change for each cutter the operations use, and a rapid move to each feature they cut, of the machining variables' rapid transfer distance (rapidTransferDistanceFactor x the part's box length) at the machine's own rapid traverse rate. (It replaces a flat 15 % allowance for rapids and tool changes on the cutting time: the project owner's decision of 2026-11-24.)

fields.name: Tools
fields.note: The cutters the operations use: one for each operation and cutter size (a Ø6 and a Ø8 drill are two).

fields.name: Tool Change Time
fields.note: The engine's own value, by the project owner's decision of 2026-11-24: no mill record states a tool-change time (only the gear grinders' do). Edit it for the machine.

fields.name: Feature Visits
fields.note: The features the operations cut, each one a rapid move of the tool to it.

fields.name: Rapid Transfer Distance Factor
fields.note: The machining variables' rapidTransferDistanceFactor (memory/machining/variables.csv, migration 639): multiplied by the part's box length, the typical rapid transfer distance.

fields.name: Rapid Traverse Rate
fields.note: The selected machine's own rapid traverse rate (mhr_records.specs rapid_traverse_mm_per_min, migration 1141).

fields.name: Cutting Time
fields.formula: {Facing Time} + {Rough Milling Time} + {Finish Milling Time} + {Contouring Time} + {Slot and Groove Milling Time} + {Hole Making Time} + {Edge Treatment Time} + {Other Operations Time}

fields.name: Rapid Time
fields.formula: {Feature Visits} * {Rapid Transfer Distance Factor} * {Part Box Length} / {Rapid Traverse Rate} * 60

calculators.name: Machining - Rotary Surface Grinding
calculators.description: Rotary-table surface grinding: the wheel covers the face, so each table revolution is one pass. Rough passes take the allowance down to the finish stock, one finish pass removes it, and spark-out is the reference multiple of the finish time (variables sparkOutMultiplier). Speeds and downfeeds from tblRotarySurfaceGrinding for the material.

calculators.name: Machining - Straight Bevel Gear Cutting
calculators.description: Straight bevel gear cutting: every tooth space is cut across the face width by a cutter the size of the pitch diameter (straightBevelCutterDiameterToPitchDiameterRatio), at the tblStraightBevelGearCutting cutting speed, feed per tooth and blades per side for the material and that cutter diameter.

calculators.name: Machining - Spiral Bevel Gear Cutting
calculators.description: Spiral bevel gear cutting: every tooth space is cut across the face width by a cutter the size of the pitch diameter (spiralBevelCutterDiameterToPitchDiameterRatio), at the tblSpiralBevelGearCutting cutting speed, feed per tooth and blades per side for the material and that cutter diameter.

calculators.name: Machining - Shaping
calculators.description: Gear shaping: the cutter is fed radially to tooth depth, generates the teeth in one roughing revolution, then one finishing revolution. tblShaping gives three cut types per material with no legend; type 1 (the lowest stroke rate) is read as roughing and type 3 (the finest rotary feed) as finishing. Each stroke adds the reference dwells (variables shapingDwellTimePerStroke, numDwellsPerShapingStroke).

fields.name: Rough Strokes
fields.formula: {Tooth Depth} / {Radial Feed} + pi * {Pitch Diameter} / {Rough Rotary Feed}

fields.name: Cycle Time
fields.formula: {Rough Strokes} * (60 / {Rough Stroke Rate} + {Dwell per Stroke}) + {Finish Strokes} * (60 / {Finish Stroke Rate} + {Dwell per Stroke})

calculators.name: Machining - Automated Deburring
calculators.description: Automated deburring of every sharp edge: CAD sharp-edge length at the tblDeburring edge speed of the reference default edge tool for the material.

calculators.name: Machining - Drill Press
calculators.description: Drilling on a drill press: CAD hole diameter and depth, cutting speed and feed from tblDrilling for the material and drill construction.

calculators.name: Machining - Drill Press
calculators.description: Drilling on a drill press: CAD hole diameter and depth, cutting speed and feed from tblDrilling for the material and drill construction.

calculators.name: Machining - Stock Prep Mill
calculators.description: Preparing the stock on a mill before the part is machined: the time of each milling operation group on the stock, plus the allowance for rapid moves and tool changes.

calculators.name: Machining - Stock Prep Mill
calculators.description: Preparing the stock on a mill before the part is machined: the time of each milling operation group on the stock, plus its moves from data, as the Milling station calculator times them since migration 1142: a tool change per tool (Tool Change Time) and a rapid move to each feature visited (the rapid transfer distance over the machine's rapid traverse rate). Was the cutting time plus a flat 15 % allowance (user decision 2026-11-25: the same model as the Milling station).

calculators.name: Machining - Stock Prep Lathe
calculators.description: Preparing the stock on a lathe before the part is machined: rough turning of the bar to the stock diameter, cutting data from tblGeneralTurning for the material.

calculators.name: Machining - Stock Prep Lathe
calculators.description: Preparing the stock on a lathe before the part is machined: rough turning of the bar to the stock diameter, cutting data from tblGeneralTurning for the material.

calculators.name: Machining - Stock Prep Lathe
calculators.description: Preparing the stock on a lathe before the part is machined: rough turning of the bar to the stock diameter, timed as Rough Turning is (the Machining calculator workbook's Turning sheet; cutting speed and feed from its Turning cutting conditions, the spindle capped at the machine's limit).

calculators.name: Machining - Bench Operation
calculators.description: Bench work on a machined part: identing and the spark test, each at its reference time (variables defaultIdentingTime, in seconds, and defaultSparkTestTime, in minutes).

calculators.name: Machining - Routering
calculators.description: Routering a profile: the cut length taken in passes of the depth one pass removes. The reference holds no router feed table, so the feed rate and the depth per pass are entered for the material and cutter in use.

calculators.name: Machining - Facing
calculators.description: Facing the stock square before any feature is cut: one facing pass per part.

calculators.name: Machining - Facing
calculators.description: Facing the stock piece's faces down to the part, as the Machining calculator workbook's Face Milling sheet times it: n = 1000 v / (pi D), capped at the machine's spindle limit; width passes = (face width - D / 2) / (D - 2) and depth passes = stock depth / depth of cut, each rounded up to whole passes (the sheet leaves both fractional); time = (face length + 10 mm + D / 2) / (feed per tooth x teeth x n) x width passes x depth passes, rounded up to whole seconds a face. Cutting speed and feed per tooth from the workbook's milling conditions for the material; the face mill and the depth of cut are the sheet's own. The faces and the stock on them are the stock model's: a block's top and bottom, a bar's two sawn ends. The workbook prices no face mill. (It replaces a fixed 45 s a part.)

fields.name: Cutter Diameter
fields.note: the Machining calculator workbook (memory/Machining - Calculator Database (1).xlsx), Face Milling sheet: a 60 mm face mill.

fields.name: Teeth
fields.note: the Machining calculator workbook (memory/Machining - Calculator Database (1).xlsx), Face Milling sheet: 6 teeth on the cutter.

fields.name: Range Position
fields.note: The workbook gives cutting speeds and feeds as ranges ('60 - 120' m/min). 0.5 takes the middle of each range; 0 its low end, 1 its high end.

fields.name: Max Spindle Speed
fields.note: The selected machine's own top spindle speed (mhr_records.specs spindle_speed_rpm, migration 1136). The workbook has no cap.

fields.name: Depth of Cut
fields.note: the Machining calculator workbook (memory/Machining - Calculator Database (1).xlsx), Face Milling sheet: 2 mm depth to cut in one pass.

fields.name: Approach Length
fields.note: the Machining calculator workbook (memory/Machining - Calculator Database (1).xlsx), Face Milling sheet: the length of cut plus 10 mm for the cutter's approach and overrun.

fields.name: Feed per Tooth
fields.formula: {Feed per Tooth Min} + {Range Position} * ({Feed per Tooth Max} - {Feed per Tooth Min})

fields.name: Machining Time
fields.formula: ({Face Length} + {Approach Length} + {Cutter Diameter} / 2) / ({Feed per Tooth} * {Teeth} * {Spindle Speed}) * {Width Passes} * {Depth Passes}

calculators.name: Machining - Rough Milling
calculators.description: Milling a feature's volume out (a pocket, a slot, a milled keyway): the CAD removed volume at the material removal rate of the material, most of it roughed and the rest taken at the slower finishing rate.

fields.name: Cycle Time
fields.formula: ({Removed Volume} * {Roughing Share} / {Material Removal Rate} + {Removed Volume} * (1 - {Roughing Share}) / ({Material Removal Rate} * {Finishing Rate Factor})) * 60

calculators.name: Machining - Rough Milling
calculators.description: Roughing a pocket or a flat with an end mill, as the Machining calculator workbook's End Milling sheet times it: n = 1000 v / (pi D), capped at the machine's spindle limit; width passes = (cut width - D / 2) / stepover and depth passes = cut depth / depth of cut, each rounded up to whole passes (the sheet leaves both fractional); time = (cut length + 10 mm + D / 2) / (feed per tooth x teeth x n) x width passes x depth passes, rounded up to whole seconds a cut. The stepover is the sheet's D - 2 mm, never less than half the cutter (below a 4 mm cutter D - 2 would leave the cutter overlapping itself, or no stepover at all). Cutting speed and feed per tooth from the workbook's milling conditions for the material; the cutter is the material's end mill (tblMillingFinishing), or the cut's width when walls confine it to less; the depth of cut is the sheet's own; the end mill's price and life from the workbook. (It replaces the removed volume at the material removal rate, 80 % roughed and 20 % at 0.4 of the rate.)

fields.name: Range Position
fields.note: The workbook gives cutting speeds and feeds as ranges ('60 - 120' m/min). 0.5 takes the middle of each range; 0 its low end, 1 its high end.

fields.name: Max Spindle Speed
fields.note: The selected machine's own top spindle speed (mhr_records.specs spindle_speed_rpm, migration 1136). The workbook has no cap.

fields.name: Depth of Cut
fields.note: the Machining calculator workbook (memory/Machining - Calculator Database (1).xlsx), End Milling sheet: 2 mm depth of cut on one pass.

fields.name: Approach Length
fields.note: the Machining calculator workbook (memory/Machining - Calculator Database (1).xlsx), End Milling sheet: the length of cut plus 10 mm for the cutter's approach and overrun.

fields.name: Feed per Tooth
fields.formula: {Feed per Tooth Min} + {Range Position} * ({Feed per Tooth Max} - {Feed per Tooth Min})

fields.name: Machining Time
fields.formula: ({Cut Length} + {Approach Length} + {Cutter Diameter} / 2) / ({Feed per Tooth} * {Teeth} * {Spindle Speed}) * {Width Passes} * {Depth Passes}

calculators.name: Machining - Bulk Milling
calculators.description: Milling away the volume of a feature that has no operation of its own: the same removal model as rough milling.

calculators.name: Machining - Fine Finish Milling
calculators.description: Finishing milled surfaces: a planar face's CAD area taken to the finish depth at the material removal rate, and each pocket's floor and wall finishing passes.

fields.name: Area Time
fields.formula: ({Finish Volume} * {Roughing Share} / {Material Removal Rate} + {Finish Volume} * (1 - {Roughing Share}) / ({Material Removal Rate} * {Finishing Rate Factor})) * 60

calculators.name: Machining - Fine Finish Milling
calculators.description: Finishing milled surfaces: the tool path over the CAD floor and wall area (area over the stepover) at the feed rate the finishing cutter runs in the material, plus a lead-in and lead-out per face.

fields.name: Feed Rate
fields.formula: {Spindle Speed} * {Teeth} * {Feed per Tooth per Diameter} * {Tool Diameter}

fields.name: Path Length
fields.formula: {Floor Area} / ({Tool Diameter} * {Floor Stepover Ratio}) + {Wall Area} / ({Tool Diameter} * {Wall Step-down Ratio}) + {Faces} * 2 * {Tool Diameter}

calculators.name: Machining - Fine Finish Milling

calculators.name: Machining - Contouring
calculators.description: Contouring curved walls and surfaces: a wall is followed with the side of the cutter one step-down at a time, a free-form surface with a ball cutter stepped over to the scallop height, both at the finishing feed rate of the material.

fields.name: Feed Rate
fields.formula: {Spindle Speed} * {Teeth} * {Feed per Tooth per Diameter} * {Tool Diameter}

fields.name: Path Length
fields.formula: {Wall Area} / ({Tool Diameter} * {Wall Step-down Ratio}) + {Surface Area} / {Surface Stepover} + {Faces} * 2 * {Tool Diameter}

calculators.name: Machining - Contouring
calculators.description: Contouring curved walls and surfaces: a wall is followed with the side of the cutter one step-down at a time, a free-form surface with a ball cutter stepped over to the scallop height, both at the finishing feed rate of the material. The spindle is capped at the machine's own top speed (migration 1150), not a flat 10000 rpm.

calculators.name: Machining - Perimeter Milling
calculators.description: Milling the wall of a through cutout: its CAD wall area, by the contouring model.

calculators.name: Machining - Perimeter Milling
calculators.description: Milling the wall of a through cutout: its CAD wall area, by the contouring model.

calculators.name: Machining - Perimeter Milling
calculators.description: Milling the wall of a through cutout: its CAD wall area, by the contouring model. The spindle is capped at the machine's own top speed (migration 1150), not a flat 10000 rpm.

calculators.name: Machining - Slot Milling
calculators.description: The finishing pass of each slot after it is roughed.

calculators.name: Machining - Slot Milling
calculators.description: Milling a slot out with an end mill, as the Machining calculator workbook's Slot Milling sheet times it: n = 1000 v / (pi D), capped at the machine's spindle limit; depth passes = slot depth / depth of cut and width passes = slot width / D, each rounded up; time = (slot length + 10 mm + D) / (feed per tooth x teeth x n) x depth passes x width passes, rounded up to whole seconds a slot. The depth of cut is the slotting depth ratio of the cutter, half its diameter (the sheet's example cuts 6.5 mm a pass with a 12 mm cutter). Cutting speed and feed per tooth from the workbook's milling conditions for the material; the cutter is the slot's width, or the material's end mill (tblMillingFinishing) when the slot is wider; the end mill's price and life from the workbook. The engine also times the slot by Plunge Milling and keeps the quicker. (It replaces the slot's volume at the material removal rate plus 20 s a slot.)

fields.name: Range Position
fields.note: The workbook gives cutting speeds and feeds as ranges ('60 - 120' m/min). 0.5 takes the middle of each range; 0 its low end, 1 its high end.

fields.name: Max Spindle Speed
fields.note: The selected machine's own top spindle speed (mhr_records.specs spindle_speed_rpm, migration 1136). The workbook has no cap.

fields.name: Slotting Depth Ratio
fields.note: the Machining calculator workbook (memory/Machining - Calculator Database (1).xlsx), Slot Milling sheet: it cuts 6.5 mm a pass with a 12 mm cutter (0.54 of it); half the cutter's diameter a pass.

fields.name: Approach Length
fields.note: the Machining calculator workbook (memory/Machining - Calculator Database (1).xlsx), Slot Milling sheet: the length of cut plus 10 mm for the cutter's approach and overrun.

fields.name: Feed per Tooth
fields.formula: {Feed per Tooth Min} + {Range Position} * ({Feed per Tooth Max} - {Feed per Tooth Min})

fields.name: Machining Time
fields.formula: ({Slot Length} + {Approach Length} + {Cutter Diameter}) / ({Feed per Tooth} * {Teeth} * {Spindle Speed}) * {Depth Passes} * {Width Passes}

calculators.name: Machining - Center Drilling
calculators.description: Spotting each hole before it is drilled.

calculators.name: Machining - Chamfering
calculators.description: Chamfering edges: the edge length at the tblChamfering edge speed for the material; an edge with no CAD size takes a set time.

fields.name: Cycle Time
fields.formula: {Edge Length} / {Edge Speed} + {Unsized Edges} * {Time per Unsized Edge}

calculators.name: Machining - Filleting
calculators.description: Rounding edges: the edge length at the tblCornerRoundingMill edge speed for the material; an edge with no CAD size takes a set time.

fields.name: Cycle Time
fields.formula: {Edge Length} / {Edge Speed} + {Unsized Edges} * {Time per Unsized Edge}

calculators.name: Machining - Groove Milling
calculators.description: Milling grooves: the groove length at the tblCornerRoundingMill edge speed for the material, by the filleting model.

calculators.name: Machining - Mask Cure
calculators.description: Curing the maskant before chemical milling: the cure time of the maskant in this oven (tblMaskingMaterials gives 8 h unheated and 1 h heated), shared by the parts one oven load holds.

calculators.name: Machining - Scribe
calculators.description: Scribing the maskant around each pocket to be etched: the outline of the pockets at the scribe's feed rate.

calculators.name: Machining - Etch Cell
calculators.description: Chemical milling in the etch tank: the pocket depth at the tblChemicalMillingEtchingRates rate for the material, then rinsing, desmut, desmut rinse and drying at their reference times, shared by the parts one load holds; then peeling the pocket maskant at the tblChemicalMilling rate.

fields.name: Tank Time
fields.formula: {Etching Time} + {Rinsing Time} + {Desmut Time} + {Desmut Rinse Time} + {Drying Time}

calculators.name: Machining - DeMask
calculators.description: Removing the maskant after etching: peeling the whole part at the tblChemicalMilling rate, capped at the reference time (variables demaskPeelTimeUpperCap), then dressing the pocket edges by hand (variables defaultEdgeDressingRate).

fields.name: Peeling Time
fields.formula: min({Part Surface Area} / {Peel Rate}, {Peel Time Cap} * 60)

calculators.name: Machining - Spline Rolling
calculators.description: Cold rolling a spline between racks: one rolling stroke per spline. The reference states which materials can be rolled (tblSplineRolling) and up to what module (variables splineRollingMaxModule) but holds no rolling time, so the stroke time of the machine is entered.

calculators.name: Machining - Profile Gear Grinding
calculators.description: Profile (form) grinding a gear one tooth gap at a time: the radial stock taken in strokes of the infeed, plus the finishing strokes, each stroke across the face width and its overtravel at the axial feed. The reference holds no gear-grinding table, so the grinding data of the wheel and machine are entered.

calculators.name: Machining - Threaded Wheel Gear Grinding
calculators.description: Continuous generating grinding with a threaded wheel: the gear turns one tooth per wheel start per wheel revolution while the wheel feeds across the face width, as a hob does. The reference holds no gear-grinding table, so the wheel and feed data are entered.

calculators.name: Machining - Countersinking
calculators.description: Countersinking each hole after it is drilled.

calculators.name: Machining - Part Setup
calculators.description: Loading and unloading each part on the machine, and turning it over between setups: the reference times for a part of this weight and size (componentLoadTime, variables partSetupTimeMethod weightAndSizeBased), adjusted by the reference factor and repetitions.

calculators.name: Machining - Obround Slot Milling
calculators.description: Milling a keyway that is not broached, with an end mill of the keyway's width: the cutter takes the slot in passes, each plunging its share of the depth and travelling between the keyway's two end centres, at the feed rate a cutter of that diameter runs in the material (tblMillingFinishing). The depth of a pass is the Slotting Depth Ratio of the cutter diameter: 0.2, the upper value of a tool maker's published guidance for slotting with a solid end mill of ordinary cutting edge (Mitsubishi Materials, "Depth of cut": axial depth 0.05 to 0.2 of the diameter); the reference data has no value for it.

fields.name: Slotting Depth Ratio
fields.note: The engine's own value: the reference data has none. A tool maker's published guidance for slotting with a solid end mill of ordinary cutting edge gives an axial depth of 0.05 to 0.2 of the cutter diameter (Mitsubishi Materials, "Depth of cut", mmc-carbide.com/permanent/courses/70/depth-of-cut.html); the upper value is taken.

fields.name: Feed Rate
fields.formula: {Spindle Speed} * {Teeth} * {Feed per Tooth per Diameter} * {Keyway Width}

calculators.description: Facing each end of a turned part square, as the Machining calculator workbook's Facing sheet times it: n = 1000 v / (pi D) at the bar diameter, capped at the machine's spindle limit; passes = facing stock / depth of cut, rounded up (at least one cleanup pass); time per face = (length of cut + 10 mm) / (feed x n) x passes, rounded up to whole seconds; both ends. Correction: the length of cut is the bar's radius, the tool's travel from the bar surface to the centre (the sheet types 13 mm for a 50 mm bar). Cutting speed and feed from the workbook's Turning cutting conditions (carbide, the band holding the depth of cut); tool price and life from the sheet.

Cutting speed and passes are the sheet's values; tool price and life from the sheet (no supplier source).

calculators.name: Machining - Step Drilling
calculators.description: A counterbore or a hole's larger step, drilled as the Machining calculator workbook's Step Drilling sheet times it: n = 1000 v / (pi D) at the step's diameter, capped at the machine's spindle limit; time = (step depth + 10 mm) / (feed x n), rounded up to whole seconds. Cutting speed and feed of the step diameter's band from the workbook's drilling and reaming table; drill price and life from the sheet. (It replaces a counterboring time from tblCounterboring, and 8 s a hole when that had no row.)

fields.note: The workbook gives cutting speeds as ranges ('75 - 110' m/min). 0.5 takes the middle of each range; 0 its low end, 1 its high end.

calculators.name: Machining - Internal Boring
calculators.description: Boring a hole larger than the workbook's drills reach, as the Machining calculator workbook's Internal Boring sheet times it: from the drilled diameter to the hole's, passes = (final - initial diameter) / (2 x depth of cut) rounded up; n = 1000 v / (pi D) at the drilled diameter, capped at the machine's spindle limit; time = (bore length + 4 mm) / (feed x n) x passes, rounded up to whole seconds a bore. Cutting speed from the workbook's Turning cutting conditions (carbide, the band holding the depth of cut), feed from its boring feed by hole diameter; boring bar price and life from the sheet.

fields.name: Depth of Cut
fields.note: the Machining calculator workbook (memory/Machining - Calculator Database (1).xlsx), Internal Boring sheet: depth of cut 0.5 mm.

fields.name: Range Position
fields.note: The workbook gives cutting speeds as ranges ('75 - 110' m/min). 0.5 takes the middle of each range; 0 its low end, 1 its high end.

fields.name: Max Spindle Speed
fields.note: The selected machine's own top spindle speed (mhr_records.specs spindle_speed_rpm, migration 1136). The workbook has no cap.

fields.name: Approach Length
fields.note: the Machining calculator workbook (memory/Machining - Calculator Database (1).xlsx), Internal Boring sheet: the length of cut plus 4 mm for the tool's approach and overrun.

fields.name: Passes
fields.formula: max(1, ceil(({Final Diameter} - {Initial Diameter}) / (2 * {Depth of Cut})))

calculators.name: Machining - Boring
calculators.description: Boring a hole larger than the workbook's drills reach, on a mill: timed as Internal Boring is (the workbook's Internal Boring sheet), the boring bar turning in the spindle.

calculators.name: Machining - Plunge Milling
calculators.description: Milling a slot out by plunging the end mill straight down, step after step along it, as the Machining calculator workbook's Plunge Milling sheet means it, corrected: the sheet copies the Slot Milling formula with a length of cut of 3.7 x 3.142 x 10 mm. Plunges = slot length / (plunge step ratio x D) and width passes = slot width / D, each rounded up; each plunge feeds the slot depth + 10 mm at feed per tooth x teeth x n; n = 1000 v / (pi D), capped at the machine's spindle limit; rounded up to whole seconds a slot. Cutting speed and feed per tooth from the workbook's milling conditions for the material; the end mill's price and life from the workbook. The engine times every slot both ways and keeps the quicker: plunging wins on a deep slot.

fields.name: Range Position
fields.note: The workbook gives cutting speeds and feeds as ranges ('60 - 120' m/min). 0.5 takes the middle of each range; 0 its low end, 1 its high end.

fields.name: Max Spindle Speed
fields.note: The selected machine's own top spindle speed (mhr_records.specs spindle_speed_rpm, migration 1136). The workbook has no cap.

fields.name: Plunge Step Ratio
fields.note: The engine's own value, stated in the machining workbook plan (2026-11-24): each plunge steps half the cutter's diameter along the slot. The workbook gives none.

fields.name: Approach Length
fields.note: the Machining calculator workbook (memory/Machining - Calculator Database (1).xlsx), Plunge Milling sheet: the length of cut plus 10 mm for the cutter's approach and overrun.

fields.name: Feed per Tooth
fields.formula: {Feed per Tooth Min} + {Range Position} * ({Feed per Tooth Max} - {Feed per Tooth Min})

fields.name: Plunges
fields.formula: max(1, ceil({Slot Length} / ({Plunge Step Ratio} * {Cutter Diameter})))

fields.name: Machining Time
fields.formula: {Plunges} * {Width Passes} * ({Slot Depth} + {Approach Length}) / ({Feed per Tooth} * {Teeth} * {Spindle Speed})

calculators.name: Machining - RM Composition Analysis
calculators.description: Checking the composition of each raw material lot on an XRF analyzer, as the Machining calculator workbook's RM Composition Analysis sheet times it: 60 s a lot (Time/batch), shared over the parts the lot makes. The lot is the batch: the sheet's lot is its part volume (the MOQ it states in tons is the part weight x that volume). No tool. An incoming-material inspection: the catalog's Machining Inspection process, as its own operation. (A line no quote had: HR Rates had no XRF work centre; migration 1145 adds it.)

fields.name: Time per Lot
fields.note: the Machining calculator workbook (memory/Machining - Calculator Database (1).xlsx), RM Composition Analysis sheet K5: Time/batch 60 s.
